notes: Checked: full mega-menu (no Outlet/Opruiming/Clearance/Last Chance nav item anywhere), footer nav, robots.txt/sitemap (no outlet/opruiming category slugs found in the 6.7MB product sitemap), and slug probes. /outlet (https://www.xenos.nl/outlet) 301-redirects to https://www.xenos.nl/acties, and https://www.xenos.nl/opruiming returns 404. Site search for 'opruiming' returns 9 hits but spot-checked names (a rug beater, storage boxes, a jar) are unrelated generic products -- fuzzy text-match noise, not a real opruiming/clearance concept (a nonsense-string query returns 0 hits, so the engine is not flat-default). The /acties page itself IS a genuine large PLP (H1 'ACTIES', catalog__header-count and embedded JSON both agree on 979 products, page_size 48, last_page 21, ceil(979/48)=21 consistent) but its own meta description reads: 'Bij Xenos vind je regelmatig leuke acties. Zo hebben we elke twee weken nieuwe folderaanbiedingen. Shop alle actie artikelen online op Xenos.nl.' (= 'At Xenos you regularly find fun promotions/deals. We have new flyer offers every two weeks.') -- this is explicit, unambiguous language for a rotating, time-limited promotional-flyer campaign, the textbook generic-Sale case the brief instructs to exclude, not a permanent-markdown/outlet/end-of-line listing. Its sub-links are ordinary percent-off campaigns (e.g. 'Meubels: tot 50% korting', 'Eetkamerstoelen: 20% korting', 'Java Kasten: 25% korting') with no outlet/last-chance/end-of-line taxonomy language anywhere on the page. Per the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale rule this is excluded rather than recorded, since the evidence (the page's own stated 'new offers every two weeks' cadence) resolves the question rather than leaving it genuinely ambiguous. No genuine Clearance/Outlet PLP exists on this site.
